note: Next-generation NNRTIs (fosdevirine/IDX899, doravirine, elsulfavirine) went into patients on cell-culture replication assays with a protein-binding-adjusted IC90/EC95 trough target and standard toxicology, with no animal efficacy model; the cell model's antiviral and dose predictions held for fosdevirine and doravirine, but fosdevirine's delayed-onset seizures were predicted by no toxicology species and only retrodicted in minipig.
label: HIV NNRTIs (next-generation)

engagement.model: HIV-1 replication in cell culture (MT-4/PBMC) against wild-type and NNRTI-resistant virus, with protein-binding-adjusted IC90/EC95 and in-vitro resistance selection
engagement.note: Cell-culture replication against wild-type and NNRTI-resistant HIV-1 was the class's engagement model, first public for fosdevirine (IDX899) at first-in-human; no patient comparison yet.
engagement.short: Cell-culture activity of fosdevirine, no patients yet
engagement.quote: IDX899 is a novel nonnucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) with potent in vitro activity against wild-type and NNRTI-resistant strains of human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) and with a high genetic barrier to resistance.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The in-vitro data themselves were conference abstracts (CROI 2008) and were published in full only in the 2016 J Med Chem discovery paper (10.1021/acs.jmedchem.5b01430); the 2009 first-in-human paper is the earliest tier-1 statement of the model.
engagement.judgement: The strip opens with the first member paper that states the cell model (fosdevirine/IDX899), not with a first-generation NNRTI proxy such as nevirapine: the tile's members are the three next-generation programs and older NNRTIs are not in its member list. model_filed=true because the same cell model is in the Pifeltro label section 12.4 (EC50 12 nM in 100% normal human serum, MT4-GFP cells, cell-culture resistance selection; NDA 210806); fosdevirine never filed an NDA.

engagement.model: HIV-1 replication in cell culture (MT-4/PBMC) against wild-type and NNRTI-resistant virus, with protein-binding-adjusted IC90/EC95 and in-vitro resistance selection
engagement.note: Seven days of fosdevirine monotherapy cut plasma HIV-1 RNA about 1.8 log10 at 100-800 mg: the viral-load readout the cell assay predicts moved in patients.
engagement.quote: The mean VL reductions from baseline on day 8 were 0.97, 1.87, 1.84, 1.81, and 1.78 log(10) copies/ml for GSK2248761 doses of 30, 100, 200, 400, and 800 mg QD, respectively.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (the PMC full text is not open-licensed and E-utilities returned metadata only). Doravirine repeated the comparison: Schurmann 2016 (10.1097/QAD.0000000000000876) 7-day monotherapy gave -1.37 and -1.26 log10 at 25 and 200 mg, and the 2018 Pifeltro label section 12.4 puts cell-culture-selected V106A/M, F227C and Y318F beside the same substitutions emerging in DRIVE-FORWARD/DRIVE-AHEAD failures (7 of 11 with >97-fold phenotypic resistance).
engagement.reason: Viral load fell as cell assay predicted
engagement.magnitude_basis: plasma HIV-1 RNA decline during 7-day monotherapy; the cell assay predicts activity, not a log10 effect size
engagement.judgement: Viral load is the target's own product, so the monotherapy decline is the proximal engagement readout the brief names; the paper reports patients only and does not set the cell data beside them, so comparison_stated=false with Zhou 2009 (the tier-1 statement of the in-vitro activity and adjusted IC90) as the model side. registry_date is the results posting of NCT00945282, the second (30 mg) monotherapy study; the first (100-800 mg, Idenix) study's NCT number was not located. The later target-specific confirmation (resistance substitutions shared between cell culture and doravirine trial failures, Pifeltro label 2018, tier 2, comparison stated) does not change the status and is noted here rather than entered.

dose.model: Protein-binding-adjusted cell-culture IC90/EC95 as the plasma-trough target
dose.note: Healthy-volunteer troughs at 200 mg sat four-fold above the protein-binding-adjusted IC90 trough target; no patient dosed yet, so reached but not shown enough.
dose.short: Trough 4x above adjusted IC90, no patients
dose.quote: The mean concentration at 24 h following the administration of a single 200-mg dose under fed conditions exceeded the in vitro protein binding-adjusted 90% inhibitory concentration by fourfold.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the four-fold figure is in the abstract.
dose.judgement: Dose is tied to efficacy, so a target reached in healthy volunteers before any patient was dosed is untested, not same. No tolerability margin was stated by the model in any source read (margin_stated=false). model_filed=true: the Pifeltro label carries the same yardstick for doravirine (section 12.4 EC50 in 100% normal human serum beside the section 12.3 steady-state C24 of 0.396 microM at 100 mg).

dose.model: Protein-binding-adjusted cell-culture IC90/EC95 as the plasma-trough target
dose.note: At troughs above the adjusted-IC90 target (100-800 mg) response plateaued near 1.8 log10; 30 mg, on the rising Ctau-Emax limb, gave 0.97.
dose.quote: The relationship between short-term VL change and GSK2248761 PK was best described by a maximum-effect (E(max)) model using C(τ) (E(max) = 2.0; 50% effective concentration [EC(50)] = 36.9 ng/ml).
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. That the 30 mg trough fell below the adjusted IC90 is my own arithmetic, not the paper's: Zhou 2009 puts a single 200 mg fed dose at four-fold the adjusted IC90 and Zala 2012 reports dose-proportional PK over 30-800 mg, which places 30 mg near 0.6-fold. Doravirine is consistent: Anderson 2015 (10.3851/IMP2920) 'All dose levels produced C24 h>19 nM' (the EC95 in 50% serum) over 30-750 mg in healthy volunteers, Schurmann 2016 found 25 and 200 mg equally active, and the Phase 2b (Gatell 2019, 10.3851/IMP3323) found 25-200 mg equivalent at week 24 and chose 100 mg.
dose.magnitude_basis: viral-load decline at troughs above versus below the protein-binding-adjusted IC90 trough target
dose.judgement: Called same because every dose with a trough above the adjusted IC90 was fully active and the one dose below it was half as active, so the target was reached and was enough; the trial ranked doses only in direction (magnitude=direction_only). Fosdevirine's later stop was a safety event unrelated to exposure (Margolis 2014: 'no clear association between seizures and fosdevirine plasma drug levels'), so it is scored in safety, not as a toxicity-blocked dose. No member failed for under-dosing, so contra is unavailable; elsulfavirine has no tier 1-3 dose source.

dose.model: In-silico doravirine PK model for CYP3A-inducer co-administration: nonparametric superposition of the single-dose rifabutin DDI, then a PBPK model of doravirine and its M9 metabolite, used to set the 100 mg twice-daily dose with rifabutin
dose.note: Superposition of the single-dose rifabutin DDI projected 100 mg twice daily restores efficacious troughs; the 2018 label adopted it before any twice-daily trial.
dose.short: Superposition projects BID restores troughs; untested
dose.quote: Nonparametric superposition analysis projected that administration of doravirine 100 mg twice daily with rifabutin will restore steady-state trough concentration values to efficacious levels associated with doravirine 100 mg once daily in the absence of CYP3A inducers.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Wiley full text paywalled, no PMC). The single-dose DDI itself was in healthy subjects (rifabutin cut doravirine AUC to 0.50 and C24 to 0.32 of control); the twice-daily regimen is a projection, not an observation, so the comparison is untested here.
dose.judgement: A separate track from the cell-culture trough target: that model sets what trough is needed, this in-silico model predicts what regimen reaches it under CYP3A induction, and the brief lists in-silico models used to choose doses as their own system. Opened in 2018 at the first tier-1 statement of the superposition projection (epub 2018-05-03). model_filed=true by inference: the 30 Aug 2018 Pifeltro label (section 2.2, Table 7) carries the twice-daily-with-rifabutin adjustment while its DDI table holds only the single-dose rifabutin study, and the PBPK paper calls the twice-daily trial 'subsequent', so the adjustment rested on the model at filing; the FDA clinical pharmacology review that would state this is not in the bundle (210807 MultidisciplineR 404). That is regulator reliance on in-silico data for a dosing recommendation, noted here rather than set at context level. No registry record exists for the Merck DDI trial (ClinicalTrials.gov search returned none). prediction_level=class because the model picks a regimen for a co-medicated subgroup, not which patients respond. margin_stated=false: no tolerated-exposure margin is stated.

dose.model: In-silico doravirine PK model for CYP3A-inducer co-administration: nonparametric superposition of the single-dose rifabutin DDI, then a PBPK model of doravirine and its M9 metabolite, used to set the 100 mg twice-daily dose with rifabutin
dose.note: A later trial of 100 mg twice daily with rifabutin found doravirine and M9 exposures consistent with the model's predictions; the dose adjustment held.
dose.quote: In a subsequent clinical trial, doravirine and M9 exposures, when doravirine 100 mg twice daily was coadministered with rifabutin, were found to be consistent with model predictions using rifampin and efavirenz as representative inducers.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Wiley full text paywalled, no PMC; Europe PMC lists first publication 2020-09-28). The abstract reports the confirmatory trial only as 'consistent with model predictions' and names neither its population nor the observed/predicted ratios, so subjects and magnitude are left null rather than inferred; every other doravirine DDI trial in the programme, including the twice-daily rifapentine study (Clin Transl Sci 2020, PMC7719366, which chose 100 mg twice daily 'based on nonparametric superposition predictions'), was in healthy volunteers. Rifampin and efavirenz served as the model's induction calibrators because M9 had not been measured in the earlier rifabutin study.
dose.reason: Twice-daily rifabutin dose matched PK model
dose.magnitude_basis: predicted versus observed doravirine and M9 exposure at 100 mg twice daily with rifabutin; the abstract states consistency without ratios, so no magnitude bin is assigned
dose.judgement: Called same under the dose table's 'reached, drug worked' row: the model's target was the steady-state trough of 100 mg once daily without inducers, the exposure at which doravirine passed DRIVE-FORWARD and DRIVE-AHEAD, and the source itself states that the twice-daily-with-rifabutin exposures matched the prediction (comparison_stated=true, source_calls_it=match). 'Enough' is inherited from the Phase 3 exposure the regimen was designed to reproduce; no efficacy trial on rifabutin was run and none is needed for a PK-matched regimen. Not a retrodiction: the projection (2018) and the label adjustment preceded the confirmatory trial. Year 2020 is the online publication; the trial has no registry record and no separate paper was found, so the PBPK paper is the only tier-1 record of it (trial_unreported=false because a tier-1 source reports it). The model's second use, choosing 100 mg twice daily for the rifapentine/isoniazid DDI study, is not scored: that study tested a different inducer, not the model's rifabutin prediction.

efficacy.model: HIV-1 replication in cell culture (MT-4/PBMC) against wild-type and NNRTI-resistant virus
efficacy.note: The cell-culture replication assay was the only efficacy model; no animal efficacy model was used for any member of the class.
efficacy.short: Cell replication assay; no animal efficacy model
efficacy.quote: IDX899 is a novel nonnucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) with potent in vitro activity against wild-type and NNRTI-resistant strains of human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) and with a high genetic barrier to resistance.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; see the engagement opener for why the 2009 first-in-human paper carries the model statement.
efficacy.judgement: Cell culture, not an animal, is the efficacy model the class relied on (the Pifeltro label's microbiology basis is cell culture alone); no humanized-mouse or macaque study was found for any member, so the cell is not empty and there is one track.

efficacy.model: HIV-1 replication in cell culture (MT-4/PBMC) against wild-type and NNRTI-resistant virus
efficacy.note: The Phase I/IIa monotherapy studies' viral-load endpoint responded as the cell assay predicted; doravirine later carried the same prediction through Phase 3 non-inferiority at 84%.
efficacy.quote: GSK2248761 at 100 to 800 mg QD for 7 days was well tolerated, demonstrated potent antiviral activity in treatment-naive HIV-infected subjects, and had favorable PK and resistance profiles.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The abstract does not label viral-load change as the primary endpoint in so many words; it is the antiviral-activity endpoint the two studies were designed around, so endpoint_role=primary. Elsulfavirine's 48-week Phase 2b versus efavirenz (NCT02489461; 81% vs 73.7% <50 copies/mL) exists only as a CROI 2017 abstract and a Viriom press release, tier 5, and is consistent but not entered.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: viral-load decline on monotherapy and proportion <50 copies/mL at week 48; the cell assay predicts activity, not an effect size

patient_trials.quote: Because a dose-response relationship was not identified, a second study examined a lower, 30-mg QD dose in 8 subjects (6 active and 2 placebo).
Doravirine monotherapy demonstrated robust antiviral activity at both dose levels, without evidence of viral resistance, and was generally well tolerated.
At week 48, 321 (84%) participants in the doravirine group and 306 (80%) in the darunavir group achieved plasma HIV-1 RNA of less than 50 copies per mL
At week 48, 84.3% (307/364) of DOR/3TC/TDF recipients and 80.8% (294/364) of EFV/FTC/TDF recipients achieved <50 HIV-1 RNA copies/mL (difference 3.5%, 95% CI, -2.0, 9.0).
Trials were halted when 5 treatment-experienced subjects (1 receiving fosdevirine 100 mg, 4 receiving fosdevirine 200 mg) developed new-onset seizures after ≥4 weeks of exposure to fosdevirine.

efficacy.judgement: The first member comparison with a patient primary endpoint is fosdevirine's 2012 monotherapy paper; doravirine's DRIVE-FORWARD (Molina 2018) and DRIVE-AHEAD (Orkin 2019) Phase 3 non-inferiority results are consistent and sit in patient_trials rather than as new entries, as does the fosdevirine Phase 2b halt, which was for seizures, not for lack of effect. No NNRTI member failed in patients for efficacy, so neg and contra are unavailable; outcome_tested is null because viral load is the accepted surrogate and no outcome trial was run. Elsulfavirine is a member but has no tier 1-3 patient source.

safety.model: Nonclinical toxicology in standard species (rodent plus non-rodent; monkey per Castellino 2013) as filed for fosdevirine and later doravirine
safety.note: Fosdevirine entered humans on a standard toxicology package whose species no tier 1-3 source names; healthy volunteers to 1,200 mg were clean, no patient comparison.
safety.quote: IDX899 was well tolerated; and no serious adverse events, dose-dependent adverse events, or laboratory abnormalities were detected.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The quote is the healthy-volunteer outcome, not the animal data; the first-in-human paper is the earliest tier-1 evidence that a toxicology package existed and was silent, and no source read names its species.
safety.judgement: Opener only, as a proxy for a package no public document describes; the status is untested regardless. model_filed=true on the track because doravirine's package is in the Pifeltro label (section 8.1 rat/rabbit embryo-fetal at 9x/8x human exposure, section 13.1 mouse/rat carcinogenicity, rat fertility), whereas fosdevirine's IND toxicology was never published in a review.

safety.model: Nonclinical toxicology in standard species (rodent plus non-rodent; monkey per Castellino 2013) as filed for fosdevirine and later doravirine
safety.note: Five of 35 treatment-experienced patients had delayed-onset seizures (SONNET) that no toxicology species predicted; monkey CNS carried parent drug, not the patients' conjugate.
safety.quote: The CNS disposition and metabolism of Fosdevirine (FDV), an HIV non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor, was investigated in four patients who unexpectedly experienced seizures after at least 4 weeks of treatment in a Phase IIb, HIV-1 treatment experienced study.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (ACS full text paywalled; Firecrawl returned the abstract only). The IND toxicology species are not named in any tier 1-3 source read; Castellino 2013 examined rabbit, minipig and monkey samples. Margolis 2014 (10.3851/IMP2689, epub 2013-10-24) gives the clinical account: 'Trials were halted when 5 treatment-experienced subjects ... developed new-onset seizures after >=4 weeks of exposure' and calls the finding 'without precedent in antiretroviral drug development'. Doravirine's own package (rat, mouse, rabbit; Pifeltro label sections 8.1 and 13.1) was clean and its patients were too (DRIVE-AHEAD: fewer neuropsychiatric events than efavirenz), a same that does not outrank this contra on the track.
safety.magnitude_basis: new-onset seizures in 5 of 35 fosdevirine-exposed subjects versus none predicted by any toxicology species
safety.judgement: Scored contra because seizures are a harm rodents, dogs and monkeys can show and the package was silent ('unexpectedly'); counted once, here rather than in dose, because the model stated no margin and the seizures were not exposure-related. Year is the Castellino epub (2012-12-20), the earliest public comparison of species with the seizure patients; the registry record NCT01199731 (SONNET) posted results only in 2017 and its 2011 termination notice ('stopped due to safety concerns') is not a results posting. model_filed=null for this entry because fosdevirine has no FDA review; the population was NNRTI-resistant treatment-experienced patients, still unselected by any biomarker. The seizures were seen only in the treatment-experienced study (SONNET) and not in the naive study (SIGNET) or the monotherapy studies.

safety.model: Minipig CNS disposition and MALDI-imaging study run after the fosdevirine seizures (retrodiction)
safety.note: Run after the seizures: the cysteine-conjugate metabolite dominating seizure patients' CSF also dominated and persisted in minipig white matter, unlike monkey.
safety.quote: This metabolite persisted in the CNS for an extended period of time after the last dose in both seizure patients and minipigs.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (ACS full text paywalled). Whether minipigs themselves seized is not quotable from the abstract, whose closing sentence refers to 'species differences in CNS toxicity/seizures observed after FDV dosing'; the match scored is the CNS metabolite predominance and persistence, so source_calls_it=partial.
safety.magnitude_basis: CNS cysteine-conjugate metabolite predominance and persistence after the last dose, patients versus minipig
safety.judgement: A separate track from the standard species because the minipig study was built after the clinic knew the answer (decision 10): it reproduced the human CNS metabolite finding, so retro, never same. It made no prospective prediction for any later member, so no fresh entry follows. Rabbit also carried the conjugate as the predominant component but the abstract reports persistence only for minipig and patients, so rabbit is not given a track.
